machine: generic small-part injection tool (not a specific press)
description: Injection molding, polypropylene, small precision parts (click pens, cases). The additive rules are turned OFF rather than set to zero: overhang and bridging are not manufacturing limits when the melt fills a closed cavity. Draft, wall and hole aspect are the governing geometry; fill/pack, sink, warp and gate location remain handoffs.

source.ref: PP nominal wall ~0.8-3mm; below 0.8 is a local feature that needs fill analysis

wallMinMm.detail: Small parts can run 0.6mm locally, but that is a decision backed by a fill study, not a default.

source.ref: steel-safe minimum for small PP parts
below ~0.3 the shut-off flashes; it is a tooling feature, not a part feature

gapMinMm.detail: A declared zero-gap fit is not judged by this rule (the contract tolerance is the ruler).

overhangDeg.reason: No support concept: the melt fills a closed cavity, so a down-facing face is not a manufacturing limit. Judging a molded part by an FDM overhang rule was a wrong ruler, not a conservative one.

bridgeMaxMm.reason: A bridge is an unsupported span in additive; in a mold the cavity supports the melt.

source.ref: core-pin L/D; long small cores deflect and wear
typical 1-2 deg per side for PP; textured faces need more

draftMinDeg.detail: Evaluated by the best-pull-direction draft solver; undercuts that cannot be pulled are reported separately. Dense meshes can exceed the solver budget; that is reported as undetermined, never as a pass.

escapePassageMinMm.reason: Venting is a tooling detail (parting-line vents, ejector-pin vents); trapped gas is a fill/pack handoff, not a part-geometry rule.

source.ref: PP shrinkage 1.5-2%; achievable tolerance depends on dimension and tool

tolMm.detail: A capability, not a geometric fact: excluding on it needs a requirement declared elsewhere.

source.ref: polished PP tool; texture is a tool decision

surfaceRaUm.detail: Reported for information only. Never used to exclude.

notes: The click-pen rotor was excluded by fdm-pla-0.4 for a 217.8mm2 overhang that injection molding does not have. This profile replaces that ruler, not the measurement: the 0.36mm wall is still below 0.8 and still fails, which is a real design question rather than a process mismatch.
